Definition: Atsel, the name of an Israelite, and of a place in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Two bearers share this name, and the record keeps them apart. One is Azel the son of Eleasah, a Benjamite named in the family lists of Saul's house, and the other is a place, the valley of Azal, to which the people will flee in the day the LORD goes forth to fight.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two Azels show how one name can hold a family and a refuge at once, and the valley that shelters the fleeing is as real as the man who bore the name.
RelatedPeople: Azel, Son of Eleasah; King Saul
